name: Two Hundred
description: 200 (Deux Cents) is a point-trick partnership card game from Canada, especially popular in New Brunswick. Four players use a 36-card deck (2s, 3s, 4s, 6s removed). Teams bid in increments of 5 (50-100); highest bidder names trump and must make their bid. First team to 200 points wins.

overview.description: 200 (Deux Cents) is a point-trick partnership card game from Canada, especially popular in New Brunswick. Four players use a 36-card deck (2s, 3s, 4s, 6s removed). Teams bid in increments of 5 (50-100); highest bidder names trump and must make their bid. First team to 200 points wins.

history.origins: Likely originated in Canada; played in New Brunswick for at least 3-4 generations (1930s or earlier). Closely related to Rook (Parker Brothers 1906); possibly Rook was based on 200 or both share a common ancestor.
timeline: 1930s or earlier: Played in New Brunswick for at least 3-4 generations; closely related to Rook (Parker Brothers 1906).

setup.dealing: All cards dealt (9 each); bidding then play.

rules.objective: First partnership to reach 200 points wins. Bid for the right to name trump; make your bid to score, or lose the amount.
rules.gameplay: Bidding (50-100 in 5s); highest bidder declares trump and leads. Follow suit; highest trump or led-suit card wins trick. Aces 10 pts, 10s 10 pts, 5s 5 pts (100 pts per deal).
keyRules: Make bid to score it; fail and lose that amount

strategy.basic: Bid on strong hands: aces, 10s, 5s (point cards), and long or void suits. Unbalanced distribution (long suits, at least one void) is desirable. Make your bid to score it; fail and your side loses the bid amount.
strategy.intermediate: Track important cards (point cards and trumps) and which have been played. Remember opponentsâ€™ holes (voids). When your partner is winning a trick, throw them point cards to maximise team score.
strategy.advanced: Bidding: identify hands with aces, high cards, and sequences. Defence: try to force the bidder to lose point cards or trump. Communication through card play (leading high to show strength, etc.).
tips: 100 points per deal (A-10-5 count); bid 50â€“100 in 5s.
Strong bids need point cards and trump length or voids.
When partner leads and will win, discard aces, 10s, or 5s to them.
Also known as Deux Cents, Dix, Bidder 10, Le Rough, La Bloutte, La Fouine.
